scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) fr %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "1000000000: un milliard;", "1000000000000: un billion;": French counts in the long scale, so "billion" is 10^12.; TLFi, BILLION: "B. — Un million de millions (10^12)."; Académie 9e éd., BILLION: "Rare. Mille millions. Synonyme vieilli de Milliard. Selon un décret de 1961, le mot Billion a reçu une nouvelle valeur, à savoir un million de millions (10^12), qui n'est pas entrée dans l'usage." The two dictionaries disagree on the use of "billion", so a number with "billion" carries its scale, and the short scale reads it as "mille millions".

group_mark.source: CLDR 48 fr number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1 234 567,5"): the narrow no-break space groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR 48 fr number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1 234 567,5"): the comma marks the decimals.

space_groups.source: CLDR 48 fr number symbols: digits are grouped with a space, so "1 000 000" is one number.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "des millions de personnes" names no number; "deux millions" does.

scale_noun_agrees.source: A scale noun agrees in number with its count. Académie française, "Questions de langue", Nombres: "vingt et cent varient devant millier, million, milliard, qui sont des noms et non des adjectifs numéraux : deux cents millions d’années"; Académie 9e éd., MILLION: "Sa fortune s'élève à plusieurs millions d'euros." "Mille" is a numeral, not a noun, and stays invariable.

joiner_tens_units.source: TLFi, VINGT: "La conj. et ne s'emploie que pour joindre un aux dizaines: vingt et un [...] Except.: quatre-vingt-un [...] V. aussi soixante et onze"; reading accepts "et" or a hyphen.

joiner_after_hundred.source: TLFi, CENT: "un n'est pas relié à cent par et" (except the old "cent et un").

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) fr %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "1001: mille >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;"; "mille et un" keeps "et" in set phrases ("Les Mille et Une Nuits"); reading accepts both.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: Académie 9e éd., MILLE: "Dans cet emploi on dira mille et un, mille et une, plutôt que mille un, mille une.": "et" after "mille" goes before "un" only, so a well-formed last group after "mille et" is below a hundred.

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF fr data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2100: "mille cent", "deux mille cent": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: The CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) fr-FR rules quoted for joiner_between_groups write no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

minus_idioms.source: TLFi (CNRTL), "moins" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/issue-fixes/163/sources/tlfi-moins.txt): "À tout le moins, tout au moins, pour le moins": "En estimant les choses au minimum"; and "Dans le décompte de l'heure, précédant le nom de nombre correspondant au nombre des minutes manquant": "Cinq heures moins un quart... Cinq heures moins cinq". After an hour, written as "heure", the symbol "h", "midi" or "minuit", "moins" counts the minutes before it, so "midi moins dix" is no -10. "au moins deux" is "at least two", not -2: in these idioms "moins" is an adverb.

number_noun.source: TLFi, "numéro" 4: "Numéro un, loc. adj. ou subst.", "c'est l'ennemi numéro un (Camus, Peste, 1947)". The word after "numéro" names the number, so "numéro un" is the number one, not the article. TLFi, "nombre" A 1 b: "Concept caractérisant une unité, une collection d'unités ou une fraction d'unité. Allevy transforme les chiffres en figures, le nombre 1 s'exprimant par une tour, 2 par un oiseau, 3 par un chameau, ainsi du reste (Flaub., Bouvard, t. 1, 1880, p. 124)". The word after "le nombre" names the number, so "le nombre un" is the number one.

percent_phrase.source: TLFi, "cent": "Pour cent unités. Abrév. % (cf. pourcentage). Augmentation de six pour cent; taux d'intérêt de trois pour cent par an." So "cent" after "pour" names the percent sign, not the number 100.

noun_after_count.source: TLFi (CNRTL), "second": "Second et deuxième peuvent être empl. l'un à la place de l'autre, sauf dans les syntagmes figés, les loc. et les adj. numéraux ordinaux comp. (où second n'est jamais empl.)". After a count, "secondes" is the unit of time: "dix secondes" is 10 and the noun.

article_one.source: "un" and "une" are also the indefinite article; alone before a noun they are a weak number ("j'ai acheté une maison").

of.source: "un million de personnes", "deux milliards d'euros": "de" after a scale noun; a plural collective after it multiplies the count ("deux millions de douzaines"). fr.wiktionary "du": "Article contracté, formé de la préposition de et de l'article le."; "des": "Contraction de l'article défini du pluriel les avec la préposition de."

fraction_of.source: "un tiers de douzaine": a fraction of a collective noun multiplies it, as in pt-PT "um terço de dúzia".

denominator_particle.source: French has no particle like pt "avos".

class_noun.source: No French class noun is read.

half_unit.source: "et demi" follows the noun in French ("un kilo et demi"), so no unit takes a half before it.

lone_decimal_mark.source: Structural, no external source: a group mark stands only between digits, so a point right before the first digit marks decimals, as in pt-PT: ".5" is 0.5. CLDR 48 fr number symbols: decimal ",", so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Académie 9e éd., ENTRE: "Pour mesurer approximativement une grandeur par référence à un minimum et à un maximum. La statue mesurait entre trois et quatre mètres. Cela vous coûtera entre mille et deux mille francs."

roman_series_noun.source: A noun that marks a place in a series makes the Roman numeral beside it an ordinal (Wikipedia, "Roman numerals": "Capital or small capital Roman numerals are widely used in Romance languages to denote centuries."; "Book volume and chapter numbers, as well as the several acts within a play."; "World War I and World War II"). Each noun, from en.wiktionary.org: French "siècle": "century (period of 100 years)"; French "chapitre": "chapter"; French "volume": "volume (of a book, a written work)"; French "tome": "tome, volume"; French "partie": "part (portion, amount)"; French "acte": "act"; French "scène": "scene (all senses)"; French "concile": "(religion) council"; French "guerre": "war"; French "dynastie": "dynasty".

roman_title.source: A regnal title before a name makes the Roman numeral after the name a regnal number (Wikipedia, "Regnal number": "Regnal numbers are ordinal numbers—often written as Roman numerals—used to distinguish among persons with the same regnal name who held the same office, notably kings, queens regnant, popes"). Each title, from en.wiktionary.org: French "roi": "king"; French "reine": "queen (a female monarch)"; French "pape": "Pope"; French "empereur": "emperor"; French "impératrice": "empress".

roman_word.source: A Roman numeral that is also a word or a common abbreviation reads only after a strong cue ("Play CD" holds no 400). Each word, from en.wiktionary.org unless another dictionary is named: French "CD": "CD (compact disk)"; French "CV": "initialism of curriculum vitæ"; Translingual "XL": "(chiefly clothing) extra large (the manufactured size)"; Translingual "mm": "(metrology) Symbol for millimetre (millimeter), an SI unit of length equal to 10−3 metres (meters)."; Translingual "cm": "(metrology) Symbol for centimeter (centimetre), an SI unit of length equal to 10−2 meters (metres)."; Translingual "ml": "(metrology) Symbol for millilitre, an SI unit of fluid measure equal to 10−3 litres."; French "mi": "(music) mi, the note 'E'".
